findings.found: <input type="text" name="phone" id="phone">: autocomplete="phone": "phone" is not an autofill token; did you mean "tel"?
findings.fix: use on, off, or the tokens of the HTML Standard in their order, such as "shipping postal-code" or "work email"; the message suggests the token that was probably meant

basis.text: an autocomplete value is on, off, or in this order an optional section- token, an optional shipping or billing, an optional contact type before a contact field, one field name from a fixed list and an optional webauthn
the purpose of a field that collects information about the user can be determined by software, in HTML with the autocomplete tokens (H98), and an incorrect value is failure F107
basis.source: Understanding SC 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (W3C WAI, WCAG 2.2)

findings.own: an autocomplete attribute on an input that is not hidden, a select, a textarea or a form whose value is not on, off or a list of autofill tokens in the order of the HTML Standard; on a form, only on and off are valid; an empty value is the default and is not reported

findings.found: <input type="email" name="email" id="email">: aria-describedby names the id "email-hint", which no element of the file has
findings.fix: point the attribute at the id of the element that holds the label, the hint or the error message, or give that element the id; an error message that is added later must get the id the field already names

basis.text: an error message sits at or near its field, is tied to it with aria-describedby, and aria-invalid marks the field in error
aria-errormessage names the id of the element that holds the error message of a field marked with aria-invalid, and aria-describedby is the more widely supported way to tie the two
a label with a for attribute labels the first element in tree order with that id, if it is labelable; a label without one labels its first labelable descendant; a hidden input is not labelable

findings.own: an aria-describedby, aria-errormessage or aria-labelledby that names an id no element of the file has, a label whose for names no element, an input whose list names no element, and a field whose form attribute names no element; ids added by a script later are not seen

findings.found: <input type="password" name="password2" id="password"> has no programmatic label: no label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, title or placeholder names it
findings.fix: add a visible <label for="id"> with the id of the field, or wrap the field and its text in a label; where no visible label fits the design, name the field with aria-labelledby pointing at visible text, or with aria-label

basis.text: every user interface component has a name and a role that software can determine, and a form control with no programmatically determined name is failure F68
basis.source: Understanding SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (W3C WAI, WCAG 2.2)

basis.text: autocomplete takes space-separated tokens on input, select, textarea and form, browsers may ignore off on login fields, and fitting tokens meet WCAG 1.3.5

findings.own: a field whose type (email, tel, password), name or id points to a purpose of the autofill list, such as a name, an address, an email address, a phone number or card details, that has no autocomplete field name: no autocomplete attribute, or on, or off on a field that is not a login field; WCAG 1.3.5 covers fields about the user, and the tool cannot tell whose data a field asks for

findings.found: <input type="text" name="lastName" id="last-name"> is required, but its label, description and legend show no asterisk and no word required
findings.fix: say it in the label or the legend, as text such as (required) or an asterisk explained at the top of the form

basis.text: a required field is marked with the required attribute, with aria-required for assistive technology, and with text such as (required) in its label for everyone
among the sufficient techniques, a required control is shown as required in the text of its label or legend (H90)
basis.source: Understanding SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (W3C WAI, WCAG 2.2)

findings.own: a field with the required attribute or aria-required="true" whose label text, aria-labelledby text, aria-describedby text and the legend of its fieldset hold no asterisk and no word required; a note, because a line such as "all fields are required" elsewhere on the page is not seen

findings.found: <input type="checkbox" name="terms"> is required, but its label, description and legend show no asterisk and no word required
findings.fix: say it in the label or the legend, as text such as (required) or an asterisk explained at the top of the form

basis.source: Understanding SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (W3C WAI, WCAG 2.2)

findings.own: a field with the required attribute or aria-required="true" whose label text, aria-labelledby text, aria-describedby text and the legend of its fieldset hold no asterisk and no word required; a note, because a line such as "all fields are required" elsewhere on the page is not seen

findings.found: <select name="station" id="station"> holds 36 options, more than 30, with no hint linked by aria-describedby
findings.fix: consider a text field with a datalist or a search, grouping the options with optgroup, or a hint that typing the first letters jumps to an option

basis.text: a datalist gives a text field suggested values while the person can still type, an alternative to scrolling a long list, with accessibility limits of its own
aria-describedby ties extra instructions, such as the expected format, to a field, and they are read after its label

findings.own: a select element with more options than optionLimit (40 by default) and no aria-describedby that points at text, which counts as a search hint whatever it says; a note for the UX audit, because a long list is slow to scan and a script may already make it searchable
